Fire, Health & Safety Consultant - Contractor/Associate

Ark Workplace Risk | Competitive Day Rate 

 

At Ark Workplace Risk, we empower our clients to confidently manage risk, compliance, and safety through a trusted partnership built on expert knowledge, innovative solutions, and proactive guidance and insight.

 

About Ark Workplace Risk: 

Proven Expert Knowledge: With over 30 years of experience and a trusted reputation among 200+ UK organisations, we provide workable solutions that align with our clients' organisational and business goals, as well as regulatory requirements.

Industry-Leading Software: Our innovative tools streamline risk and compliance management, putting clients in control and enabling them to demonstrate accountability to stakeholders.

Insight-Driven Solutions: As industry thought leaders, we provide actionable insights into emerging legislation, guidance, and industry trends, ensuring court-readiness for their business.

Responsive Partnership: From every day, business-as-usual guidance to urgent, critical, complex, and contentious scenarios, we work in partnership with clients, becoming their trusted advisor and solution provider, whenever and wherever they need us most.

 

Responsibilities: 

 

  • Undertake risk assessments including fire and health and safety, ensuring the fee earning target is met. 
  • Undertake various fire, health and safety assignments within your competency.
  • Deliver client reports within the agreed SLA, in accordance with a forensic and pragmatic approach to ensure the Ark 'Gold Standard' is achieved. 
  • Design health and safety site management systems where required, specific to client requirements.
  • Undertake onsite briefings and advise on risk management improvements.
  • Work collaboratively with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders.
  • Work with other consultants to ensure we are constantly sharing knowledge across the team.
  • Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of controlling risks, compliances etc. in relation to our online management system QUOODA®

 

The ideal candidate will have:

  • At least 2+ years' fire, health & safety risk assessment experience within the built environment in residential and/or commercial buildings
  • Good working knowledge of Approved Document B
  • Good working knowledge of BS 9999 / 9997
  • Education suitable to be competent to carry out Fire and Health & Safety risk assessments on seven or more floors
  • The ability to undertake Fire Risk Assessments and General Risk Assessments at the same time
  • Articulate and clear communicators and report writing abilities as well as a comprehensive understanding of current UK regulations

 

Qualifications

  • Must have NEBOSH General Certificate in Health & Safety or equivalent as minimum.
  • Must have a minimum of a level 3 in fire safety/fire risk
  • Recognised fire safety memberships e.g. AIFireE, MIFireE, GIFireE, MIFSM etc.
  • Willing to apply for or have registered on any of the following fire risk assessors registers IFSM, FRACS, IFPO or IFE

 

Practical Requirements: 

Ability to facilitate hybrid working with home office that is suitable for connectivity to the office and clients, a safe and productive place to work conducive for delivering daily duties.

Nivoda started with a simple observation: buying and selling diamonds was slow, opaque, and inefficient, no matter how big or small your business was. Our platform fixes this by giving every jewellery business, wherever they are in the world, the same access to inventory, financing, and logistics as the biggest players in the industry.

As we expand into jewellery and new markets, the complexity of moving products across borders has grown fast. Loose diamonds have historically had simple customs treatment in most jurisdictions; jewellery is a different story, with its own tariff regimes and duty rules. This is a new, dedicated role that will sit within fulfilment, close to the shipments and the broker relationships where trade compliance actually gets executed day to day preparing documentation, applying classifications, managing broker performance, and owning our duty drawback program end to end.   • Prepare all shipment documentation and commercial invoices, and ensure accurate, complete documentation is retrieved from brokers and carriers and stored centrally on our platform

  • Apply the HTS classifications and country-of-origin determinations that Legal & Compliance have approved, consistently across our shipment processes and systems in partnership with product

  • Manage day-to-day customs broker relationships, coordinating clearance, reviewing broker performance, and ensuring broker practices stay aligned with our classification framework

  • Monitor duties as part of landed shipping costs, catch unexpected duty outcomes, and file claims with customs brokers when errors are found

  • Resolve routine customs queries during clearance, and ensure declarations for import and export are applied accurately

  • Own the duty drawback program day to day, acting as the internal point of contact with Livingstone, and preparing and validating claims before submission

  • Partnering with our manufacturers (starting with India) to ensure their export documentation and processes support compliant, duty-efficient shipping

  • Identifying and acting on duty-saving opportunities through relevant free trade agreements (e.g. India-UK, EU-UK, EU-India, UAE-India)

  • Building out trade compliance processes as our jewellery business scales into new duty-liable markets, and escalating complex classification or legal interpretation questions to Legal & Compliance

  • Proven experience in global trade compliance or customs operations, with a track record on US, UK, EU import/export specifically

  • Direct experience managing customs broker relationships and shipment documentation at volume

  • Experience filing duty drawback or tariff reclaim claims

  • Comfortable working as an individual contributor with real autonomy

  • Detail-oriented and process-minded: you'll be establishing how this works at Nivoda, not just following an existing playbook

  • Based in the EU or UK, with the flexibility to work across time zones as we scale globally

  • Strong stakeholder management skills, coordinating external brokers/carriers/manufacturers and internal Legal, Fulfilment, and Ops teams

  • A commercial mindset, you connect compliance work back to cost savings and business impact

Nice to have ✨

  • Experience with free trade agreements and preferential duty schemes (e.g. India–UK, EU–UK, EU–India, UAE–India)

  • Experience in jewellery, diamonds, gemstones, or other high-value/luxury goods logistics

  • Background in a fast-scaling, international e-commerce or marketplace business
